title: totalBudget() and runwaySeconds() use inconsistent accounting bases, producing views that cannot be reconciled
description:
`totalBudget()` returns `rewardToken.balanceOf(this) + dispatcherHook.mintDebt()`, while `runwaySeconds()` uses `rewardBudget + dispatcherHook.mintDebt()` divided by `rewardRate`. These bases disagree: `balance == rewardBudget + totalDebt + dust`, not `rewardBudget` alone. Neither view projects pre-settlement `_updatePool` accrual either.

The net effect: `totalBudget` over-reports (includes earmarked user debt); `runwaySeconds` under-reports (uses `rewardBudget` that hasn't been settled for elapsed time). Any monitoring logic that multiplies `runwaySeconds * rewardRate` and compares to `totalBudget` will never reconcile.
impact: View-only; monitoring dashboards and keeper logic see persistent numerical mismatch. No funds at risk.
proof: Deploy, fund the pool, let a staker accrue unclaimed reward over time, read both views. `totalBudget()` includes the staker's accrued-but-unclaimed reward (in balance but not in rewardBudget); `runwaySeconds()` uses rewardBudget and excludes it. The two figures disagree by `totalDebt`.
suggested-fix: Align both views: either both use `rewardBudget + dispatcherHook.mintDebt()` (exclusive of earmarked debt), or both use `balance + mintDebt` (inclusive). Add NatSpec clarifying semantics. For `runwaySeconds`, project `_updatePool` first so the runway reflects current-instant accrual rather than stale state.
consolidation-note: No ES overlap. Standalone view-consistency issue.
sanitizer-note: View-only inconsistency; QA-tier. These views are used externally (exposed via the public ABI), not unused — so the C4 'unused view functions' rule does not fully apply. Keep as Low.
